svg.title: Reed-Solomon encode and decode with three data and two parity shards
svg.desc: The systematic generator matrix of the code with k = 3 and m = 2, its Cauchy parity rows F4 8E 01 and 47 A7 7A, the parity it produces for the data pinned by ReedSolomonTest, and a decode after losing shards s0 and s3 that inverts the remaining rows 1, 2 and 4 and recovers the data.
svg.text: Reed-Solomon with k = 3 data and m = 2 parity shards
Every byte is an element of GF(2^8); the values are those pinned by ReedSolomonTest.keepsTheEncodingMatrixStable
Rows 0–2 are the identity, so the data passes through.
Parity row r, column c holds 1 / ((k + r) XOR c).
Decode after losing s0 and s3
First byte of d0: A6·10 ⊕ F5·FF ⊕ 04·06 = B2 ⊕ AA ⊕ 18 = 00
The decoder then re-encodes s3 and s4 from the recovered data, so every slot is filled again.
Any 3 of the 5 rows are invertible, because every square submatrix of a Cauchy matrix is.
